# Repository-wide Copilot instructions

- Preserve Maestro's canonical lifecycle: GROUNDING → MOMENTUM → MASTERY → REPETITION → GROUNDING.
- Momentum and Repetition are stages, not agents. Specialist roles are capabilities within stages.
- Treat project adapters under `projects/` as optional integration records; do not redefine Maestro or make its core depend on any one adapter.
- Preserve source-of-truth boundaries: project code, domain evidence, decisions, and canonical backlogs remain in their owning project unless explicitly migrated.
- Prefer coherent system-level changes and explicit interfaces over isolated patches.
- Do not fabricate tool execution, test results, independent reviews, evidence, or workflow transitions.
- Keep consequential actions (publishing, sending, spending, merging, deploying, deleting) behind explicit authorization.
- For historical or research data, retain exact sources, scope, uncertainty, and unknown values; never invent missing transaction details.
- Run relevant tests and validators; report exactly what ran and what did not.
